info.name: WSO2 Motor Rally API
info.description:
The rally game engine (backend/api/openapi.yaml).

## Setup

1. Start the service: `set -a && source config.env && set +a`, `make docker-db`, `make run`.
2. Send **Health / Liveness probe** to confirm `{{baseUrl}}` is reachable.
3. Run the folders top to bottom. Every request that creates something stores its id in a collection variable, so the next request already points at it.

## Auth

Two identities share this API and the collection models both.

- **Organizer** — collection-level Bearer `{{organizerToken}}`. Locally the service runs with `TOKEN_VALIDATOR_ENABLED=false`, so it decodes organizer claims without checking the signature. The collection pre-request script mints a token that satisfies that mode when `organizerToken` is empty. **Against any deployed environment, paste a real Asgardeo id token into `organizerToken` instead** — the minted one will be rejected.
- **Crew** — the *In-car (crew)* folder overrides auth to Bearer `{{teamToken}}`. `POST /sessions/join` is unauthenticated and mints that token; its test script stores it. Every phone in a car joins the *same* session and gets its own token, so re-running **Join vehicle** for a second crew member is a normal flow, not a conflict.

## Not covered here

`GET /ws` is a WebSocket upgrade, which a REST collection cannot carry. Open a Postman WebSocket request against `ws://localhost:8080/ws?topic=event:{{eventId}}` (organizers) or `topic=session:{{sessionId}}` (crews), passing the same bearer token. Contract: `backend/api/asyncapi.yaml`.

Every non-2xx body is exactly `{"message": "..."}`.

exec: // Mint a local-dev organizer token when none is set.
// authz.DecodeOrganizer, which checks only that the issuer is not
// rally-team, that exp is in the future, and that sub is present —
// the signature is never verified. So a dummy signature is enough
const token = b64url({ alg: 'HS256', typ: 'JWT' }) + '.' + b64url(claims) + '.local-dev-only';
console.log('Minted a decode-only organizer token. Local dev only — replace it for any deployed environment.');

item.name: Tasks
item.description: Attaching a task to a waypoint lives at the end of this folder rather than under *Routes & waypoints*: it needs both a waypoint and a task, so it can only run once the task exists.

request.description:
Tasks are data, never new code paths: one row per challenge, scored by the `type`'s validator in `internal/taskengine`.

`type` is one of `INPUT_SELECT`, `INPUT_NUMBER`, `MULTI_SELECT`, `SCAN_BARCODE`, `TELEMATICS`, `GEOFENCE_CROSS`, `PROXIMITY`, `GRID_FILL`, `BLIND_TIMER`, `BRANCH`, `REST_LOCK`, `TIMED_TRIVIA`, `GATE_MATCH`.
`trigger`: `geofence` | `sensor` | `choice` | `manual` | `timed`.
`sensor`: `none` | `geolocation` | `devicemotion` | `camera` | `qr`.

The scoring keys inside `config` differ per type and are stripped when a crew reads the task:

| type | scoring config | crew submits |
|---|---|---|
| `INPUT_SELECT`, `TIMED_TRIVIA` | `answer` (+ `limitSec`) | `{"answer": "…"}` |
| `INPUT_NUMBER` | `answer`, `tolerance` | `{"answer": 42}` |
| `MULTI_SELECT` | `answers` | `{"answers": ["…"]}` |
| `GRID_FILL`, `GATE_MATCH` | `solution` | `{"answer": ["…"]}` |
| `SCAN_BARCODE` | `payload` | `{"payload": "…"}` |
| `BLIND_TIMER` | `targetSec` | `{"elapsedSec": 60.2}` |
| `BRANCH` | `solvePoints`, `skipPoints` | `{"branch": "solve"}` |
| `TELEMATICS` | thresholds | `{"hardStops": 2, "sharpTurns": 5, "km": 31.4}` |
| `GEOFENCE_CROSS`, `PROXIMITY` | `checkpointId` | `{"reached": true}` |

A duplicate `code` within the event is a 409.

Provisions the vehicle and its crew roster in one call. The crew ids returned here are what a phone picks from at join time, and each member's `phoneNumber` is what the last-four check on `POST /sessions/join` is verified against — a member with no number on file can never join. A duplicate `code` within the event is a 409.

`filters.query` matches the vehicle code or the team name, anywhere in the value and ignoring case; `filters.routeId` narrows to one course. Both are optional, and the empty strings above match the whole fleet.

The returned `totalCount` counts what the filter matched, not the fleet, so a filtered table pages through its own results.

item.name: In-car (crew)
item.description:
The phone's surface. Every request here authenticates with `{{teamToken}}`, not the organizer token — the folder overrides collection auth.

Run **Join vehicle** first: it is the only unauthenticated write and it is what issues the token. The event must be published.

request.description:
The zero-facilitator start: no one hands out credentials, the crew picks their own vehicle, and joining is what authenticates the phone.

`crewMemberId` is chosen from the vehicle's own roster; `phoneLast4` is the last four digits of that member's number as the organizer entered it, which is the only thing standing between a stranger and someone else's car.

**Every phone in the car joins the same session.** The first to arrive creates it and the rest attach to it — each gets its own device row and its own team token, and `crew` in the response is who else is already aboard. There is no one-phone-per-vehicle conflict; send this again with a second `crewMemberId` to model a second phone.

Failure modes: 409 if the event is not `active` (publish it first), 404 if the member is not on this vehicle's roster, 403 if the last four digits do not match. The 403 never says which half was wrong.

**The server decides what a position means.** The phone only reports where it is; the backend evaluates every boundary and answers with what unlocked plus any lifecycle events (`geofence`, `rest_lock`, `trivia`, `arrival`).

The first ping starts the run. A position inside the finish geofence auto-finishes it and issues the voucher. Pinging a finished session is a 409.

The same endpoint the organizer edits through, but `tasks.RedactForCrew` strips the scoring keys — `answer`, `answers`, `solution`, `payload`, `targetSec`, `tolerance`, `solvePoints`, `skipPoints`, `checkpointId` — before the definition reaches a phone. Rendering a task never reveals it.

The body shape is per task type — see the table on **Tasks / Create task**. The example matches the sample `INPUT_SELECT`.

Scoring happens server-side and cannot exceed the task's `points`; the phone never decides whether it was right. Resubmitting **corrects** the total rather than adding to it. Submitting on a finished session is a 409.
Files the same kind of alert an organizer would, tagged `source=crew` and carrying the vehicle's live position.
The manual fallback — arriving inside the finish geofence does this automatically. Finishing twice is a no-op. Locks the score and issues the voucher.

item.name: Cleanup
item.description: Destructive requests, kept last so a top-to-bottom run does not delete the vehicle that the Alerts and In-car folders still need.

request.description:
Corrects provisioning; it does not retire a car mid-rally.

Sessions, submissions, scores and alerts all hang off the vehicle row by a cascading foreign key, so this is refused with a **409 once the vehicle has any session** — deleting one then would erase a result rather than fix a typo. The crew cascades away with the vehicle.

Run it after the *In-car (crew)* folder and you should get the 409, which is the interesting case.
